text:
maria: quick q — we land a couple of safetensors sharding patches. for sparse layers (row-sparse / block-sparse) should warmup be lazy by default or aggressive prefetch? thinking about memory blowups on 48GB GPUs

raj: my vote is lazy by default. sparse shards can be huge and most models touch only a small fraction at infer time. aggressive prefetch risks OOMs + longer cold-starts overall :thinking_face:

ellie: lazy makes sense but we need a clear programmer UX for 'hotstart this layer' when a critical route needs the perf. maybe an explicit hint API or attribute in the manifest?

tim: +1 to ellie. also consider a fallback policy: try lazy, but if tail latency > SLO for X minutes, promote to eager warmup for the offending shards. keep quota on eager warmup so a single tenant doesn't starve others.

maria: that matches my concerns. UX proposal: manifest entry per weightgroup with fields: "warmup": "lazy|eager|hint", "priority": int, "eviction": "pct|lru". default lazy, can be overridden by model-owner or rollout. example: 

```json
{"weights": [{"name":"attn_kv","format":"safetensors","shards":4,"warmup":"lazy","priority":5}]}
```

raj: keeping it in the manifest is good. small nit: "priority" semantics need doc—higher number = earlier warmup? also how does this interact with sharding strategy (replicated vs partitioned)?

ellie: replication vs partitioning should be orthogonal: manifest hints apply per-shard replica. if partitioned, promotable shards must respect data locality (don't warmup remote shard to avoid cross-node fetches).

maria: good point. we should expose two separate knobs: warmup_intent (owner hint) and warmup_policy (cluster-enforced) so infra can override to protect capacity.

tim: infra-enforced policy idea: a token-bucket for eager warmups per node, and a circuit-breaker that drops eager warmups when memory pressure > threshold. also autoscale signal could temporarily increase bucket.

prefetch-bot: queued warmup job for model:rlhf-chat-v3, shards: 12, mode: lazy -> scheduled in 30s

raj: edge-case: safetensors files with huge contiguous buffers (embedding tables) still may need special streaming loader to avoid copy+map overhead. recommend we keep a streaming path that maps large tensors via mmap even when using safetensors index.

ellie: agree. so final action items: (1) add warmup fields to manifest schema (maria), (2) doc precise priority semantics + examples (raj), (3) infra work: token-bucket + circuit-breaker for eager warmup (tim), (4) implement mmap/streaming for large tensors (ellie). I'll make a short RFC follow-up with sketches.

maria: thanks — I'll draft the manifest patch and a tiny compat layer so loaders ignore unknown fields. keeping lazy default. :thumbsup:

raj: sounds good. if you want I can prototype the token-bucket sim in python to pick thresholds.

ellie: ping me on the RFC when it's up, happy to review the loader patches.

maria: will do.
